T439 (managent inbox --ack with no target reads other consoles' mail, and no record says who read it) — verified, hardened, audited; the code fix itself was already committed by T441 while T439 sat unclaimed since 2026-08-08T15:22:30Z. THE FIX IS IN HEAD: commit 2849ef8 (T441, 2026-08-08) introduced the targetless-ack guard, the --all opt-in, and read_by/read_at on acks. T439 verified that fix against the bundle's three asks, extended the regression to the bundle's exact bars, audited the live ledger, and (as of this file) the only thing between the task and a clean close is the done-gate's 'tracked and clean' check on src/managent/main.zig, which the working tree carries DIRTY with another task's (T364's) in-flight uncommitted reap work (T364's console was live at 2026-08-20T03:29Z, runner PID 86265, --max-wall 2700; the T439 fix is committed, the dirt is not T439's). Per the AGENTS.md rule for defects already fixed, the regression asserts the invariant rather than re-observing the bug red.

BUNDLE ASK 1 — SCOPE THE ACK. DECISION (recorded here per the bundle's 'decide and state which'): a targetless --ack is REFUSED with usage — exit 1, 'error: inbox --ack without a target would mark every row's directives read. Use inbox <target> --ack to ack one row, or inbox --all --ack to ack all.' Display-only (no --ack) stays targetless-legal. The opt-in is explicit --all; there is no silent path and no silent ack-nothing path (arm 12 proves --all still acks). The residual `target.len == 0` term inside the ack-match condition (main.zig, ack rewrite) is now unreachable dead logic — the guard above it makes target.len==0 imply all_flag — and is harmless; it was left untouched because the file carries T364's uncommitted edits and T439 does not write that file.

BUNDLE ASK 2 — RECORD THE READER. The ack rewrite writes read:true + read_by + read_at, where read_by resolves from the same identity path claim/done use: MANAGENT_TASK_ID env → PI_MODEL env → 'unknown' (resolveAckIdentity, main.zig:1446). Reading is backward compatible: readDirectives (main.zig:5181) parses only the read bool, so a bare `"read":true` from a pre-fix record still parses and still filters out of resume/inbox — the append-only ledger was NOT rewritten (43 old records keep their bare form; see ask 3). Strings go through writeJsonString on the rewrite (T399), so an escaped-quote note survives the ack round-trip.

BUNDLE ASK 3 — RE-DELIVER WHAT WAS WRONGLY CONSUMED + LEDGER AUDIT. Audit of docs/infra/managent/directives.jsonl (the only directives ledger; DIRECTIVES_FILE main.zig:5163): 75 records carry read:true; 32 carry read_by (read_at window 2026-08-08T17:08:57Z → 2026-08-20T03:10:22Z — the earliest attributed ack predates the T441 commit by 10 min, i.e. the fixed binary was in use at cutover); 43 are BARE — read:true with no read_by/read_at, send-ts window 2026-08-01T20:28:03Z (D007/T226) → 2026-08-08T15:12:01Z (D068/T437), every one acked before the fix cutover. REPORTED COUNT: 43 directive records whose read cannot be attributed from the ledger. Of those, exactly ONE is documented as cross-consumed by a targetless ack: D068 (addressed to T437) was consumed by the T427 console's targetless ack — the T427 console's own transcript noted D068 was not its own, and the orchestrator's T437 post-close amendment (2026-08-08T15:47:39Z) records the mechanism. The other 42 are indistinguishable from correctly-targeted acks — the ledger is structurally blind to who read them, which is the defect itself. docs/infra/managent/archive.json holds 0 directive records (nothing to attribute there). RE-DELIVERY OF D068: deliberately NOT performed, because the substance was already delivered — T437 (done 2026-08-08T15:44:55Z) polled its inbox unprompted and acknowledged D068 before the cross-ack; evidence on disk in docs/infra/managent/tasks.json (T437 verdict_note 'D068 acknowledged'; orchestrator amendment 'T437 polled its inbox unprompted and logged D068 (falsifying my prediction that it would not)'). Flipping D068 back to read:false would misstate the record (T437 did read it) and would plant a permanent false STALL on a done row in every resume surface; the append-only ledger is left untouched. The defect that matters is the one the fix closes: no future read can be unattributed.

BARS — TEST-FIRST REGRESSION, BOTH ARMS. tools/regression-inbox-loop.sh gained TOTHER in the seeded scratch kanban and three arms: 10 (SEEDED, the bar's first arm) plants one directive per row, attempts a targetless --ack, requires the refusal, then asserts on disk that NEITHER row's directive carries read:true and that the display still lists both — the pre-fix code would have consumed both and failed the disk check; 11 (NULL, the bar's second arm) runs a properly targeted ack (inbox TSEED --ack) and asserts exactly 'acked 1 directive', read_by:T439 on the TSEED record, the TOTHER record still bare-unread on disk, and TOTHER's inbox still listing its mail — a fix that acks nothing fails this arm, so the pair cannot both pass by doing nothing; 12 proves the --all opt-in acks the remaining mail after the refusal. All 12 arms PASS against the deployed known-good binary bin/managent (built 2026-08-20T02:56Z from committed HEAD). Deliberately NOT rebuilt from the working tree: src/managent/main.zig carries T364's in-flight uncommitted edits (reap verb + resume fleet-stalls), and building that tree would risk a broken binary and clobber a live console's work. The script is already wired into `zig build test` (build.zig:337).

INBOX-LOOP: polled bin/managent inbox T439 --ack at claim, at findings-write, and at close; empty at every poll (no directives acked, no D0NN to record).
